subject.title: telegram: isolated-ingress handler-timeout dead-letters a user message silently (no reply, no replay, nothing surfaced)

question: For Telegram isolated-ingress failed tombstones, should OpenClaw preserve terminal dead-letter semantics with visibility/notification, or automatically replay handler-timeout rows that had zero attempts?
rationale: The source-level failure is clear, but the permanent behavior affects duplicate delivery, reply-fence cleanup, retry policy, operator diagnostics, and Telegram user messaging, so maintainers need to choose the product contract before an automated fix is safe.

options.title: Surface And Notify Failed Tombstones
options.body: Preserve terminal failed rows for unsafe timeout and retry-limit cases, add failed-ingress operator visibility, and send one duplicate-safe failure notice when a user message is dead-lettered.

options.title: Replay Handler-Timeouts Once
options.body: Allow a guarded one-time replay for handler-timeout rows with zero attempts, but require proof that late original handlers cannot duplicate replies or session effects.

options.title: Operator Visibility Only
options.body: Expose failed tombstones in status or doctor without Telegram user notices, accepting that senders may still see silence while operators get a repair path.

recommendation.title: Surface And Notify Failed Tombstones
recommendation.body: Preserve terminal failed rows for unsafe timeout and retry-limit cases, add failed-ingress operator visibility, and send one duplicate-safe failure notice when a user message is dead-lettered.

likelyOwner.reason: joshavant authored the earlier spooled replay and stalled isolated spool handler lifecycle work that frames the duplicate-safety versus replay tradeoff.
